chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, the people most entitled to wish wealth for others are the misers, because when people become self-sufficient, they refrain from seeking their wealth. And the people most entitled to wish righteousness for others are the people of faults, because when people become righteous, they refrain from pursuing their faults. And the people most entitled to wish forbearance for others are the people of foolishness, those who need their foolishness to be pardoned. Yet the people of miserliness come to wish for the poverty of others, the people of faults come to wish for the defects of others, and the people of foolishness come to wish for the foolishness of others. And in poverty is the need for the miser, in corruption is the seeking out of the private faults of the people of defects, and in foolishness is requital by sins.

key_terms.السَّفَهِ: foolishness, rashness, and lack of sound judgment
key_terms.الْبُخَلَاءُ: the miserly people who withhold wealth
key_terms.الْحِلْمَ: forbearance and restraint in dealing with others
key_terms.عَوْرَةِ: a person's exposed fault or vulnerability

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say that misers, the flawed, and the foolish should wish good for other people?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a moral inversion: those who most benefit from the good condition of others are often the very ones who wish the opposite for them. It condemns miserliness, fault-finding, and foolishness, and calls attention to how poverty, corruption, and rashness feed harmful social behavior.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5862 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), peace be upon him, who said:

"Indeed, the people most deserving to wish for others to be wealthy are the misers because if people become self-sufficient, they will refrain from seeking their wealth.
And the people most deserving to wish for others to be righteous are those with flaws because if people become righteous, they will stop pursuing their faults.
And the people most deserving to wish for others to be forbearing are the foolish, for they need others to pardon their foolishness.
Yet, the misers wish for people to be poor, the flawed wish for others to have faults, and the foolish wish for others to be foolish.
In poverty lies the need for the miser, in corruption lies the exposure of the flawed, and in foolishness lies the reciprocation of sins."
